title: Preventing SQL Injection with Parameterised Queries
summary: SQL Injection occurs when untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query. Use parameterised queries and prepared statements to separate code from data.

steps: Identify all database query call sites that use string concatenation or template literals.
Replace concatenated values with parameterised placeholders ($1, ?, :name depending on the driver).
Pass user inputs as bind parameters in an array or object.
Enable strict mode / prepared-statement caching where supported.
Add integration tests that attempt injection payloads and verify they are safely escaped.

title: Mitigating Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in React Applications
summary: XSS attacks inject malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users. In React, avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML and always sanitise user-generated HTML content.

steps: Audit all uses of dangerouslySetInnerHTML across the codebase.
Replace with sanitised rendering using a library like DOMPurify.
Implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) header to mitigate impact of any remaining XSS.
Escape user input when rendering outside of JSX (e.g. in document.title or URL parameters).
Add automated tests with XSS payloads (e.g. <script>alert(1)</script>) to confirm proper escaping.

title: Secure JWT Verification – Preventing Algorithm Confusion
summary: JWT algorithm confusion attacks exploit libraries that accept the 'none' algorithm or allow the attacker to switch between HMAC and RSA. Always specify the expected algorithm explicitly.

steps: Explicitly set the allowed algorithms array to only the algorithm you sign with (e.g. ['RS256']).
Never include 'none' in the algorithms list.
Validate the 'iss' and 'aud' claims to ensure the token was issued by a trusted party.
Rotate signing keys periodically and use JWKS for key management.
Reject tokens that do not pass signature verification with a 401 response.
